final_codebook.domain: Rational number arithmetic (fraction and mixed-number subtraction)

skills.name: Convert to improper
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number or whole number as an equivalent improper fraction (or as a fraction with a specified denominator) to enable fraction operations.
inclusion_criteria: A step rewrites a mixed number a b/c as (a·c+b)/c
A step rewrites a whole number n as an equivalent fraction n = (n·d)/d to match a needed denominator
exclusion_criteria: Only finding/choosing a common denominator (e.g., LCM) without converting a mixed/whole number
Only scaling a fraction a/b to an equivalent fraction with a new denominator when no mixed/whole-number conversion is involved
Only performing subtraction after forms are already compatible

skills.name: Find common denominator
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) for unlike fractions to prepare for subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly computes an LCM or otherwise selects a target common denominator for two different denominators
A step states the chosen common denominator before (or while) rewriting fractions
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and no denominator-selection work is done
Only multiplying numerator and denominator to rewrite a fraction after the common denominator has already been chosen

skills.name: Scale equivalent fractions
skills.definition: Rewrite one or more fractions as equivalent fractions by multiplying numerator and denominator to reach a chosen common denominator.
inclusion_criteria: A step rewrites a/b as (a·k)/(b·k) to match a specified common denominator
A step shows both quantities expressed over the same denominator as a result of scaling
exclusion_criteria: Only selecting the common denominator (e.g., computing LCM) without performing the rewriting
Only converting mixed/whole numbers to improper fractions without scaling to a new denominator
Only subtracting once denominators already match

skills.name: Subtract and simplify
skills.definition: Compute the difference once quantities are in compatible form and express the result in an acceptable simplified form.
inclusion_criteria: A step subtracts numerators over a common denominator (x/d − y/d)
A step subtracts whole and fractional parts separately and recombines
A step reduces a resulting fraction to lowest terms and/or converts between improper fraction and mixed/whole-number form as the final presentation
exclusion_criteria: Only converting inputs (mixed↔improper or choosing/scaling denominators) without computing the difference
Only choosing a common denominator or scaling to equivalent fractions without subtracting
Purely restating the final answer with no computation or simplification action

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01 (minor wording refinement to include whole-number-to-fraction with specified denominator).
decisions.reasoning: C01 has 3/3 consensus and is diagnostically distinct from denominator alignment and subtraction.

decisions.details: Kept C02 as S02 (denominator selection/LCM only).
decisions.reasoning: C02 has 3/3 consensus and separates the decision of a common denominator from the mechanical scaling step, improving tagger reliability.

decisions.details: Kept C03 as S03 (equivalent-fraction scaling to the chosen denominator).
decisions.reasoning: C03 has 3/3 consensus and captures a distinct operation that is often a source of errors even when the LCM is known.

decisions.details: Merged C04 + C05 into S04 ('Subtract and simplify').
decisions.reasoning: Although both had 3/3 consensus, the final codebook must contain exactly 4 skills; subtraction and final simplification/formatting are tightly coupled in these dossiers and can be reliably annotated together as the post-alignment execution phase.

summary: Consolidated five fully-consensus candidates into exactly four skills by keeping the three preparation skills (conversion, common-denominator selection, and scaling) and merging the two end-stage skills (subtraction and simplify/format) into a single execution skill to satisfy the 4-skill constraint while preserving clear, distinct cognitive operations.
